To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the leakage current increase of hadron irradiation is independent of material and can be described by the universal annealing behavior.

the leakage current increase of irradiated silicon detectors can be parameterized with a universal function of fluence, temperature and annealing time, and that the fluence dependence of this function is almost independent of material parameters like resistivity, impurity concentration or oxygen precipitation.
the current-related damage is independent of the starting material and is of intrinsic origin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the material on the radiation hardness of silicon detectors.
the development of a model for the annealing behavior of leakage currents in irradiated silicon detectors which allows the calculation of the current after irradiation and annealing.
the question whether the leakage current of irradiated detectors is determined by material parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for all investigated silicon detectors, the leakage current increase is mainly caused by intrinsic defects, which are independent of the initial impurity concentration and resistivity.
the leakage current behavior of irradiated silicon detectors depends on the irradiation source but is independent of the starting material of the detector.

for all investigated material the leakage current increase is determined only by the fluence and the irradiation temperature, but not by the initial impurity concentration or resistivity of the material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the leakage current of silicon detectors is determined by the concentration of intrinsic defects and is almost independent of material properties.

the leakage current increase of irradiated silicon detectors is determined by a single parameter, namely the fluence of the fast neutrons, and is almost independent of all material related parameters.
the leakage current increase of irradiated silicon detectors is independent of the starting material and can be described by the same parameterization for all material.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the annealing behavior of the leakage current of irradiated silicon detectors is a material-independent property which is not influenced by the initial impurity concentration and resistivity of the silicon.
the annealing behavior of the leakage current is the same for all investigated material, independent of their impurity concentration.
for a precise prediction of the leakage current increase after irradiation the material dependence of the damage parameter alpha can be neglected.
